subject: Command Bridge: EdgeRetail throughput & latency incident
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgeretail.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeRetail: Elevated inference latency and 5xx rate

Hi Jordan / Team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency for our checkout personalization calls starting ~08:50 PDT. 95th pct latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.9s and 5xx rate spiked to ~4.8% (was ~0.1%). This is affecting live traffic on us-west-2 and causing visible failures on the checkout page.

We rolled back our client-side retry changes (no impact) and throttled traffic for a single region which reduced error rate slightly but didn't restore normal latencies. Can you confirm whether this is an infrastructure issue on Redwood or if a model/serving change is implicated?

Attaching a short sample of request IDs and timestamps (attached as incident_logs_0412.zip). Happy to open a bridge — we need an ETA and a mitigation plan.

Alex Morgan
Head of Engineering, EdgeRetail
alex.morgan@edgeretail.com

Attachments: incident_logs_0412.zip

Date: 2027-04-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeRetail: Elevated inference latency and 5xx rate

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the sample IDs. We are standing up an exec command bridge now. Join here: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210 (bridge) 

Immediate plan:
- 09:30 PDT: Bridge (ops + SRE + model runtime) — we will run triage and look at kernel/runtime metrics, KV cache behavior, and model variants.
- If root cause = runtime pressure, we will spin additional capacity in us-west-2 and failover traffic to a warm pool.
- If root cause = model variant regression, we'll rollback to the pinned model and enable the fallback route.

We're treating this as high priority and will update every 30 minutes on the bridge. Team on call: Steph (runtime), Marcus (SRE), Laura (customer comms).

Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec escalation — EdgeRetail incident (initial triage)

Looping in leadership briefly — this is escalating toward an exec view given EdgeRetail's traffic profile and visible customer impact. Quick notes from initial checks:

- Error spike appears correlated with a surge in median sequence length for a subset of requests (checkout-recommendation route) between 08:48–09:05 PDT.
- us-west-2 GPU queues saw multiple long tail deque times (runtime queuing > 800ms).
- No config rollouts on our side in the last 24 hours; infra autoscaling looks healthy but needs manual capacity bring-up to recover latency SLO.

Action items for bridge:
1) Auth: Steph to pull per-node KV cache hit/miss and token distribution (10m).
2) SRE: Marcus to warm additional dedidcated instances in us-west-2 and prepare routing rules to shift 30% traffic.
3) Comms: Laura to prepare customer-facing status message with ETA window and mitigation steps.

If we cannot achieve recovery within 45 minutes, request approval to enable a temporary model fallback (approx +10% token cost) and route to a quantized variant.

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, SRE Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgeretail.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Command Bridge: findings and temporary mitigation in place

Status update from the bridge (11:05 PDT):

Summary of findings so far:
- Root cause: observed KV cache thrashing driven by a sudden pattern of long prefix prompts in the checkout-recommendation requests. This increased KV cache misses and forced more full-token generation, spiking runtime work per-request.
- A small percentage (~7%) of requests used a new client-side feature that concatenates dynamic debug metadata into prompts; these requests accounted for ~60% of the increased token volume.
- No code rollouts on Redwood; client change at EdgeRetail triggered the shift.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- We throttled/blacklisted the debug-metadata prefix at the routing layer for EdgeRetail traffic (rolled at 10:55 PDT) — error rate dropped to ~0.6% and 95th pct latency moved back to ~480ms.
- Marcus spun up 6 additional warm instances in us-west-2 to reduce queueing.
- Enabled fallback to the quantized variant for the troublesome route as a precaution.

Attachments attached: perf_snapshot_0412.png (heatmap of queue times), incident_logs_0412.zip (sample request IDs).

Next steps / customer commitments:
- We will continue to monitor for 4 hours and run a focused regression test with their devs to ensure the client-side debug flag is removed from prod requests.
- Laura will send a formal status note to EdgeRetail with the timeline and action items.

-stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Runtime & Inference Optimizations
Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-13T02:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary / customer commitments — EdgeRetail outage 2027-04-12

Alex / Priya — thanks again for your patience on the bridge. Below is a concise post-incident summary and our next steps.

Incident timeline (all times PDT):
- 08:48 — Latency & 5xx spike observed by EdgeRetail and reported to Redwood.
- 09:15 — Initial triage; bridge stood up at 09:30.
- 10:55 — Routing rule applied to block debug-metadata prefix; partial recovery observed.
- 11:05 — Fallback quantized model enabled; warm hosts added; 95p latency stabilized ~480ms.

Root cause: A customer-side feature that appended dynamic debug metadata to prompts increased average token counts for a subset of requests, causing KV cache thrashing and long runtime queueing.

What Redwood did:
- Applied routing rule to remove problematic prefix for live traffic.
- Brought additional warm capacity to reduce queueing pressure.
- Enabled short-term fallback to a compatible quantized model variant.
- Collected targeted logs and perf snapshots (attached).

Customer commitments and follow-ups:
1) EdgeRetail devs will push a client hotfix to strip debug metadata from production requests (ETA: 24 hours).
2) Redwood will run a joint regression test with EdgeRetail devs in a staging window (scheduled: Apr 13, 09:00 PDT).
3) Redwood will deliver a postmortem doc and action plan with long-term mitigations (prefilled autoscaling and a prefix-detection alert) within 72 hours.

We're treating this as a priority accelerator for our product improvements around prefix-detection heuristics; Marcus and Steph will lead the engineering follow-up. Laura will send the public-facing status note to your ops channel in 30 minutes.

If you need anything before the regression run, ping me directly.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
